introduction:
# Current Calor language reference

Write .calr files. Bodies use two-space indentation and structural blocks end at dedent.
Declarations use lowercase space-separated headers. Functions use func and →; public is the default.
Types use C# names, T[] arrays and T? nullability. Binding and parameter types precede names.
Use let for immutable bindings and var for mutable bindings; set performs updates.
Expressions use infix operators with C# precedence and expression-valued postfix calls/indexing.
Effects (!) and postconditions (=>) occur before the first body statement. result is the body result.
Collection iteration uses each; counted loops use for, with distinct snapshot and reevaluated forms.
Plain strings interpolate ${expression}; \${0} preserves literal placeholder text.
Use declaration /// documentation. Tooling owns source identities; do not write declaration IDs.
Do not handwrite raw C# passthrough; converters own byte-counted raw payloads.
The optional namespace follows the module label: module FileLabel Contoso.Tools.
Omitting the namespace means the global namespace; the module label is not a namespace.
Token-count decisions do not by themselves establish semantics or a measured full-reference budget.
overview:
## Calor Language Overview

Module, class and function bodies use indentation and lowercase, space-separated headers.
Functions use func, type:name parameters and → returnType; public visibility is the default.
Types and members include class, record, interface, property and this[...] indexer declarations.
Use let for immutable bindings, var for mutable bindings and set for updates.
Control flow includes if/else if/else, while, each collection iteration and two distinct for modes.
Contracts and authoritative effects describe obligations and side effects with requires, => and !.
Async functions distinguish their body result from the callable Task or ValueTask carrier.
Expressions use C# precedence, postfix calls and indexing. Collections use ordinary .NET types.
Types use C# names, T[] arrays and T? nullability. Literals include 42, true, "hello" and 18.00m.
Query a specific feature for complete examples; use action=features for conversion support.
agentInstructions:
Calor is an indentation-only DSL that compiles to C# on .NET 10.

### MANDATORY Rules for AI Agents

Rule 0: Read `calor://primer` once before writing Calor. Use `calor_help` with `query` or `feature` for details; `action=features` reports conversion capabilities.
Rule 1: Never create new `.cs` files. All new code MUST be written in Calor; new files must be `.calr` files.
Rule 2: Convert C# to Calor before modifying: use `calor_convert`, then edit the `.calr` source. Use `calor analyze` for migration assessment.
Rule 3: Never edit generated files (`.g.cs`).
Rule 4: Compile after writing with `calor_compile` (autoFix is on by default); apply diagnostics and verify contracts with `calor_verify`.

Indent bodies two spaces; structural blocks end at dedent.
Use documented lowercase headers, func and →, without source IDs. Types precede names.
Use let for immutable bindings, var for mutable bindings and set for updates.
Effects (!) and postconditions (=>) precede the first body statement.
Expressions use C# precedence, postfix calls f(x) and indexing items[i].
Use C# type names, T[] arrays, T? nullability and exceptions for absence and failure.
Plain strings interpolate ${expression}; \${0} preserves literal placeholder text.
Bind local helpers to lambda values rather than nested function declarations.
Do not handwrite raw C# passthrough; converters own exact fallback output.

Read `calor://effects` for effect codes, `calor://tags` for syntax, `calor://id-prefixes` for tooling-owned identity, and `calor://workflows` for editing workflows. Use `calor_file_write` for atomic checked edits; for multi-file edits use `calor_session_open` and `calor_session_close`.

These are best-effort agent instructions; compiler diagnostics remain authoritative.

Convert before modifying existing C#. Agent hooks are best-effort; repository CI is the backstop for changes against a protected base.

constructs.description: Creates a new instance with ordinary constructor-call syntax. Arguments are comma-separated; a zero-argument constructor still uses (). Preserve the selected constructor and left-to-right argument evaluation.

constructs.calorSyntax: let type:name = expression; var type:name = expression
constructs.description: let declares an immutable binding; var declares a mutable binding. Both infer an omitted type. Types precede names; var is mutability, not a type-inference keyword. Give null an accurate explicit nullable type. In a match case, var name binds the matched value instead of declaring a mutable binding.
Declares a class method with the same function header as module functions. Preserve modifiers, visibility, contracts and authoritative effect rows; public is the default.

Declares a function or class method. Visibility is public by default; explicitly private and protected declarations retain their intended visibility. Parameters put the type before the name; parameter modifiers precede the type. Class methods may carry virtual, override, abstract or static modifiers. Functions inside a named static module are implicitly static.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
public static int Add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }
private void Log(string message) { Console.WriteLine(message); }

constructs.description: Creates a lambda with expression or indented statement body. An explicit effect row follows the parameters: (int:x) ! cw => body; empty ! declares a pure row. Do not write brace bodies or structural closers. The parameter-list closing parenthesis, optional row and => belong on the same line. Target delegate types and higher-order effect requirements remain authoritative; an unannotated lambda is not automatically a proof of purity.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
x => x * 2
(a, b) => a + b
items.Where(x => x > 5)

constructs.description: Declares a property with indented get, set or init accessors. Empty accessor bodies are auto-implemented; explicit bodies contain statements. Restricted accessor visibility follows its keyword, such as set private. Preserve defaults, modifiers and accessor effects.
Declares an indexer with inline typed parameters and indented get/set accessors. Preserve key order, restricted accessor visibility, defaults, modifiers and full accessor bodies.
Use bare member access for properties and fields, without parentheses. Parentheses invoke a method. Calls and indexing can chain on expression-valued receivers.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
var items = Data.Products;
var items = Data.GetProducts();

constructs.calorSyntax: for i from start to end step stepValue; for i = start; condition; i = next
constructs.description: One counted-loop keyword has two distinct semantics. The from/to/step header snapshots start, end and step once, in order, and includes the endpoint; omitted step is +1 and zero step throws. The =/semicolon form reevaluates its condition before each iteration and updates after the body or continue, not after break. Checked range overflow ends the snapshot range. Do not replace one form with the other.

constructs.calorSyntax: each item in collection; each Type:item in collection; each key, value in collection
constructs.description: Iterates synchronously over a collection with an indented body. An explicit type precedes the item name. Two names deconstruct each element without tuple parentheses; collection evaluation remains once.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
foreach (var item in items) { ... }
foreach (var (key, value) in dictionary) { ... }

constructs.description: Evaluates the condition before each iteration and executes an indented body while true.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
while (count > 0) { count--; }
while (true) { if (done) break; }

constructs.calorSyntax: if condition; else if condition; else
constructs.description: Conditional branches have indented bodies. else if and else align with if. Only the selected branch runs.
Conditional expression with two expression branches. Only the selected branch evaluates. Conditional and null-coalescing operators associate right; ordinary binary operators associate left.
Returns a value or exits a void-result body. Async body results differ from their callable task carriers; preserve that distinction.
Declares a class, public by default. Its members have indented bodies. Preserve inheritance, implemented interfaces, generic constraints, visibility and supported modifiers.

Declares an async function or class method using the async modifier.

An async declaration with scalar output `T` is callable as `Task<T>`, but its body
returns `T`. A `void` output produces `Task`. Explicit .NET `Task<T>` and
`ValueTask<T>` outputs preserve that carrier and return `T` in the body; their
non-generic forms have a void body result. Postconditions describe the body
result, not the task object. Ordinary synchronous task-returning declarations
keep their declared return type.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
public async Task<string> FetchDataAsync() { ... }
public async Task ProcessAsync() { await DoWork(); }

constructs.description:
Awaits an asynchronous operation.

Awaiting a .NET `Task<T>` or `ValueTask<T>` produces `T`. Awaiting a non-generic
carrier produces no value and cannot initialize a binding. `await` can also be
used as a statement. A custom type named `MyTask<T>` or a source declaration
named `Task<T>` is not automatically a .NET async carrier. Unsupported custom
awaitables are diagnosed or checked by generated C# validation, never inferred
from a name suffix.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
var result = await FetchAsync();
await Task.Delay(1000);

constructs.calorSyntax: try; catch ExceptionType:name when condition; finally
constructs.description: Groups an indented try body with one or more catch clauses and/or finally cleanup. Catch types, binders and filters are optional; preserve exception selection, filter evaluation and cleanup on every exit.
Throws an exception expression. Bare throw rethrows the current exception inside a catch handler, preserving its original stack rather than constructing or throwing a replacement.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
throw new ArgumentException("Invalid");
throw;

constructs.description: Declares authoritative effects in the function header-clause region before the first body statement. Empty ! is a declared pure row. An omitted callback parameter, returned-callback or delegate contract is Unknown, as is explicit ! unknown in those positions. Unknown is not permission: strict invocation fails, even when the caller declares every known effect. Transporting Unknown can report Calor0425 when a row fit cannot be proved; permissive mode waives uncertainty, never known undeclared effects. ! unknown is not a callable's own effect declaration, binding row or lambda row. Effect variables bind with <! e> and occur in rows as ! e; a scoped variable named unknown retains its identity. Parameter rows follow type:name; output rows follow the output type; binding rows precede =; lambda rows precede =>. Preserve these distinct positions. Omitted binding and lambda rows can retain effects inferred from their initializer or body; they do not mean pure. In expression position, ! is logical negation, not an effect row. An unknown external call or manifest charge is not a metadata-resolution or purity proof.

Declares a condition that must hold when the function is called. The example retains the divisor guard. A custom-message spelling is not part of this native form; use explicit exceptions when a custom failure message is required.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
// Contract.Requires(value >= 0)
// Guard.Against.Null(input)

constructs.description: Declares a postcondition before the first body statement. result denotes the body return value, including async body results rather than task objects. In expression lambdas => is the lambda delimiter, not a postcondition.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
// Contract.Ensures(result >= 0)
// Ensures non-empty result

constructs.description: Declares an invariant checked at the corresponding compilation-unit or type boundaries. Preserve the native contract AST and proof obligations, not an opaque runtime call.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: // [ContractInvariantMethod] void Invariants() { Contract.Invariant(_count >= 0); }

constructs.description: Calls a method or function with comma-separated arguments. Named arguments use name: value; ref, out and in modifiers precede values. The callee can be an expression; chains preserve left-to-right evaluation and short-circuit regions.

Declares a field with type before name, optional visibility and modifiers, and an optional initializer. Public is the default; preserve explicit private or protected visibility and readonly or static modifiers.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
private string _name;
private readonly int _id;

constructs.description: Declares an interface with indented func signatures. Preserve generic variance, inherited interfaces, effective visibility and method contracts. Explicit visibility follows the name and type parameters.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: public interface IRepository { void Save(Entity e); }

constructs.description: Declares an enumeration with indented named members and optional explicit values. Preserve the underlying CLR type; omission defaults to int.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
public enum Status { Active, Inactive, Pending }
public enum Priority : byte { Low = 0, High = 1 }

constructs.description: Declares a constructor with an indented body. Explicit visibility precedes the parameter list. A base(args) or this(args) initializer is the first body clause; preserve ordered arguments and base versus same-type delegation.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
public User(string name) { _name = name; }
public Admin(string name) : base(name) { }

constructs.calorSyntax: match expression with indented case pattern → result arms
constructs.description: Matches an expression against ordered patterns. Expression arms use → followed by a result; statement arms have indented bodies. Preserve pattern guards and use return match when returning a match expression.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
x switch { 1 => "one", 2 => "two", _ => "other" }
shape switch { Circle c => c.Area(), Rectangle r => r.Width * r.Height }

constructs.description: Null-coalescing returns the left value when non-null, otherwise the fallback. Null-conditional access reads the member only when the target is non-null.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
name ?? "default"
user?.Name
GetValue() ?? fallback

constructs.calorSyntax: using System.Text; using Text = System.Text; using type:name = resource
constructs.description:
At compilation-unit scope, imports a namespace or declares an alias. In a function body, using introduces a resource and an indented body that disposes it on exit, including exceptions. Preserve the distinction between imports and resource lifetime management.

Generated C# already imports `System`, so names such as `StringComparison` do not need an explicit `using System`. Source declarations, parameters, type parameters and aliases still participate in name lookup; the import does not override them.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
using (var stream = File.OpenRead(path)) { ... }
using var connection = new SqlConnection(connStr);

constructs.description: Declares a generic type. Put generic parameters immediately after the declaration name. Indented where clauses retain reference-type, value-type, constructor and interface constraints; generic arguments use ordinary C# type spellings.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
public class Repository<T> where T : class { }
public T Get<T>(int id) where T : new() { }

constructs.description: LINQ uses ordinary postfix calls, including generic calls and chained receivers. Bind predicates as typed lambda values and retain authoritative effect rows. Declare an IEnumerable<T> result with its accurate qualified System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable<T> type when passing it to metadata-resolved calls: unqualified interface aliases currently leave native ToArray effect resolution unknown. Do not relax effect policy or use casts to conceal that resolution boundary.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
items.Where(x => x > 5).Select(x => x * 2)
from item in items where item.Active select item.Name

constructs.description: Ordinary strings use ${expression} for runtime interpolation, including numeric expressions such as ${1}. Escape the opening marker as \${0} to keep literal placeholder text. Alignment and format clauses use ${value,4:D2}.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
$"Hello, {name}!"
$"Total: {price:C2}"
$"{firstName} {lastName}"
$"Result: {Calculate(x, y)} units"

constructs.description: break exits the nearest loop; continue proceeds to its next iteration. A C#-form counted loop still performs its update after continue.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
if (done) break;
if (skip) continue;

constructs.description: Declares a C# record class. Positional parameters retain their constructor defaults and public init properties. Indent properties and methods beneath the header. C# supplies value equality, hashing, ToString, deconstruction and with/copy behavior. Derived positional records use `record D (int:X, int:Y) : B(X)`. Record structs, partial or nested declarations and unrepresented member variants remain exact converter-owned C# fallback, not native records.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: public record Point(int X, int Y);

constructs.calorSyntax: new int[]{1, 2, 3}; new int[length]; new int[rows, columns]
constructs.description: Creates a fixed-size array with a typed initializer or explicit dimensions. Initializer elements are comma-separated expressions. Multidimensional arrays retain their rank and ordered dimension evaluation; they are not jagged arrays or lists.

Declares a named static container with a nested module. Its functions are implicitly static, so Counter.Read retains its CLR identity. The outer module labels the compilation unit; it is not the container. class Counter static is intentionally rejected. Non-static classes may still declare static members.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: public static class StringHelper { }

constructs.description: Declares a virtual class method using virtual. Derived classes may override it.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
public virtual string GetName() { return _name; }
protected virtual void OnChanged() { }

constructs.description: Overrides a virtual or abstract base method using override. Preserve the inherited signature and contracts.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
public override string ToString() { return _name; }
public override int GetHashCode() { return _id; }

constructs.description: Declares an abstract class using abstract. It cannot be instantiated directly.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: public abstract class Shape { }

constructs.description: Declares an abstract class method using abstract, without a body. Concrete derived classes must implement it.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: public abstract double GetArea();

constructs.description: Declares a sealed class using sealed. It cannot be inherited from.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: public sealed class FinalClass { }

constructs.description: Executes an indented body while holding the selected monitor. Preserve evaluate-once lock-object selection and monitor release on returns and exceptions.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: lock (_sync) { _count++; }

constructs.description: Use ordinary comments for todo items, fixmes and hacks.
Attach a declaration documentation line with the deprecation version and optional replacement. For an exact Obsolete attribute message, use the ordinary attribute form.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: [Obsolete("Use NewMethod instead")]

constructs.description: Document algorithmic complexity in an ordinary comment.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
// Complexity: O(n log n)
// Complexity: O(1) - constant time

constructs.calorSyntax: public (default), private, protected, internal, protected-internal, private-protected
constructs.description: Public visibility is the default. Write full-word visibility modifiers after the declaration name and generic parameters; compound visibility uses protected-internal or private-protected.

Declares an event, optionally with paired indented add and remove accessor bodies. Preserve the delegate type, visibility and supported modifiers. Named-module events are static; ordinary classes may explicitly declare a static event. Converter preservation of an unsupported event shape is not an authoring spelling. The complete example demonstrates declaration only. Native event subscription and unsubscription statements are not admitted yet; do not write retired section markers or invent +=/-= statements. Convert original C# when preservation is needed.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: public event EventHandler OnDataReceived;

constructs.calorSyntax: op + (type:left, type:right) → resultType; op implicit (type:value) → resultType
constructs.description: Declares an operator overload or conversion with an indented body. Conversion operators use implicit or explicit after op. An optional standalone ! effect row precedes contracts and body statements, as for functions. An explicit row is enforced and does not hide effects from callers. Direct source calls, including native enum-extension calls, preserve C# overload selection and argument mapping for implicit conversions at function, method and constructor inputs. Without a row, only intrinsic mutation and allocation are allowed; I/O, throwing and unknown calls remain rejected. The converter synthesizes explicit rows from the emitted native body. Operator effects are checked in every preprocessor configuration, up to eight condition symbols; larger conditional images fail effect checking rather than assuming purity. Preserve parameter order, result type and C# signature requirements.
Decimal literals use the m/M suffix for precise decimal values; unsuffixed fractional literals are double.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
decimal price = 18.0000m;
decimal total = 100m;

constructs.description: Single Unicode character. Uses 'char' type name directly (no abbreviation).
constructs.csharpEquivalent: char c = 'A';

constructs.description: Yields a value from an iterator or ends iteration. Preserve lazy execution, suspension, iterator disposal and cleanup; do not materialize the sequence eagerly.

Declares a delegate signature at compilation-unit or class scope. Parameters are inline; an optional indented ! row retains the delegate's effect contract. Omission and ! unknown mean Unknown, while empty ! means Pure. Unknown is not a wildcard permission or a purity proof. Callback parameter and return contracts follow the same distinction. Preserve parameter modifiers and the result type.

constructs.calorSyntax: pp CONDITION; pp elif CONDITION; pp else
constructs.description: Conditionally includes indented code. Chained pp clauses align with their opening pp. Conditions retain verbatim C# preprocessor text; preserve nested conditions and inactive branch contents under converter fidelity rules.
Declares a value type with the struct modifier. Preserve fields, properties, interfaces and value semantics rather than converting it to a reference class.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
public struct Point { public int X; public int Y; }
public readonly struct Vector2D { public readonly double X; public readonly double Y; }

constructs.description: Adds generic constraints before a declaration body. Preserve each reference/value-type, constructor, base-type and interface requirement, rather than treating a type parameter as an unconstrained object. Inside a quantified contract, where introduces its guard instead of a generic constraint.

constructs.calorSyntax: do indentedBody; while condition at the do indentation
constructs.description: Executes the body at least once. The trailing while condition is at the same indentation as do; there is no structural closer.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: do { Process(); } while (HasMore());

constructs.description: Defines part of a class that can be split across multiple files. Uses the 'partial' modifier.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: public partial class UserService { public void Save() { } }

constructs.description: Introduces an indented unsafe body. Preserve unsafe effects and compile with unsafe support; the keyword is not permission to bypass diagnostics.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: unsafe { int* ptr = &value; *ptr = 42; }

constructs.calorSyntax:
if x == null
  set x fallback
constructs.description: Use a null check and set for a conditional binding update. Assignment expressions, including ??=, are not authored expression forms.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
x ??= GetDefault();
_cache ??= new Dictionary<string, int>();

constructs.calorSyntax: Attach [@AttributeName] or [@Attr(arg1, arg2)] after a declaration header
constructs.description: Attaches metadata after the declaration header it annotates.
Express Boolean combinations with infix &&, || and unary !. These are expressions, not new pattern or block headers.
Use ordinary half-open C# ranges and index-from-end expressions inside brackets. A slice creates a new array; it is not an alias for the original array.

constructs.calorSyntax: Supported in C# → Calor migration; use if chains for handwritten decomposition.
constructs.description: During C# → Calor migration, positional and property patterns retain converter fidelity. For handwritten decomposition, use if/else if with explicit comparisons.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
(hour, minute) switch { (0, 0) => "midnight" }
obj switch { { Length: > 0 } => true }

constructs.description: Pragma directives use explicit source-ordered conversion nodes. Query calor_help action=features for current support; do not handwrite passthrough.

constructs.calorSyntax: (Type1, Type2) for types; (expr1, expr2) for literals
constructs.description: Tuple types use comma-separated types, such as (int, string). Tuple literals use comma-separated expressions, such as (1, "hello"). Named type elements are supported: (int X, int Y). A parenthesized single expression is grouping, not a tuple.
Returns left when non-null; otherwise evaluates and returns fallback. Coalescing associates right.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
var result = value ?? "default";
return name ?? "Anonymous";

constructs.description: Accesses Member only when target is non-null; otherwise returns null.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
var name = user?.Name;
var len = text?.Length;

constructs.calorSyntax: goto case expression; goto default; goto label
constructs.description: Transfers control to a constant match case, the default arm, or a label written name:. Preserve the target and surrounding cleanup; goto case does not repeat the match selector's evaluation.

constructs.calorSyntax: string.Concat(a, b); text.Substring(start, count); text.IndexOf(value, StringComparison.Ordinal)
constructs.description: String operations use ordinary C# property and method syntax. Preserve each selected overload's argument count and comparison mode. Length is text.Length; case conversion and trimming are methods. A one-character Substring is a string, while text[index] is a char. Do not invent extra arguments or replace ordinal comparison with culture-dependent behavior.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: string.Concat(a, b); text.Substring(start, count); text.IndexOf(value, StringComparison.Ordinal);

constructs.description: Characters use single-quoted literals, ordinary indexing, scalar casts and char methods. Character classification follows the corresponding .NET method, including its Unicode behavior. Do not confuse a char with a one-character string.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: text[index]; (int)value; char.IsDigit(value);

constructs.description: Use T[] for arrays and T[][] for jagged arrays. Indexing and calls can chain on expression-valued receivers. File.ReadAllLines returns string[], not List<string>.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: array[index]

constructs.calorSyntax: set target expression; set receiver[index] expression
constructs.description: Updates mutable bindings, fields or indexed storage. Indexed stores preserve left-to-right evaluate-once receiver, key and value evaluation, and dictionary updates are upserts rather than Add. Increment/decrement and compound assignment aliases are not separate expression forms. Inside a property or indexer, set declares a setter instead.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: name = expression;

constructs.calorSyntax: int, long, short, sbyte, byte, ushort, uint, ulong, float, double, decimal, string, bool, char, object, void, T?, T[]
constructs.description: Use C# type names and ordinary .NET generic types. Nullable types use a suffix (int?, string?); arrays use T[]. Integer widths and signedness use L, U or UL suffixes, decimal uses m/M and float uses f/F. Negative bounds such as -2147483648 retain their literal meaning. Absence and failure use nullability and exceptions, not dedicated Option/Result forms.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: int, long, short, byte, ushort, uint, ulong, float, double, decimal, string, bool, char, object, void, T?, T[]

constructs.calorSyntax: a + b; p && q; !p; condition ? yes : no; f(x); receiver[index]
constructs.description: Expressions use infix operators with C# precedence and postfix calls/indexing. Binary operators associate left; ?? and ?: associate right. Lazy Boolean, coalescing and conditional operands retain their evaluation regions. No legacy prefix operator or section-call delimiters are authored. Express implication as !p || q.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: a + b; a == b; p && q; !p; condition ? thenValue : elseValue

constructs.calorSyntax: forall int:i in start..end : body; exists int:i in start..end : body; forall int:i where guard : body
constructs.description: Quantified contracts retain lexical binders and native proof semantics. Ranges are half-open: start <= i && i < end, and an empty range is vacuous for forall and false for exists. Use where for other guards; runtime checking still requires supported finite bounds. Express implication as !condition || consequence, not a special operator. Do not replace quantified proofs with unmodeled CLR calls.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: // Universal/existential contracts with bounded ranges.

constructs.calorSyntax: items.Add(value); set counts[key] value; items.Count; items.Contains(value)
constructs.description: Ordinary List<T>, Dictionary<K,V> and HashSet<T> are distinct from arrays. Mutating heap collections requires mut; significant allocation requires alloc. Count reads size and Contains tests membership. Dictionary indexed updates are upserts, not Add. Preserve source-generic receiver metadata and method overloads without casts or fake types.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: list.Add(value); dictionary[key] = value;

constructs.description: Legacy section-call delimiters are retired. This migration lookup points to ordinary postfix calls, not a compatibility syntax. A manifest effect charge alone does not establish authoritative method metadata or a purity proof.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: System.Linq.Enumerable.ToArray<int>(filtered)

constructs.description: At file scope, labels the compilation unit. The optional qualified namespace follows the label; omission means the global namespace. That label is neither a namespace nor a static class declaration. A trailing block records block-namespace origin rather than file-scoped origin. Inside the compilation unit, a nested module declares a named static container with implicitly static functions.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: namespace Contoso.Tools;

constructs.calorSyntax: module ModeExtensions; func IsActive (this Mode:value) → bool
constructs.description: Enum extensions use an ordinary named static module, not a separate enum-extension container head. The receiver is the first parameter, with this before its type. Preserve the EnumNameExtensions CLR container and the extension method's static identity.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: public static class ModeExtensions { public static bool IsActive(this Mode value) => value == Mode.Active; }

constructs.description: Records a declaration's introduction version in a documentation comment immediately before the declaration. Supply one valid version. This is structured API metadata, not a runtime version check.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: // Available since version 1.0.0

constructs.description: Records a breaking change before a declaration. Supply a valid version and one C# string literal description; repeated lines retain multiple changes. Preserve the version and complete description rather than replacing them with an unstructured compatibility claim.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: // Breaking change in version 2.0.0: Description of the change

assume.name: Assume
assume.description: Documents an assumption that must be true at this point in the code.

...name: Range
...description: Represents a range value (start..end) for array/span slicing.

^.name: Index From End
^.description: Indexes from the end of a collection. Equivalent to C#'s ^n operator.

examples.name: Extension Method Parameter
examples.description: Marks the first parameter as the extension receiver.

examples.name: Default Value
examples.description: Declares a parameter with a default value.

examples.name: Out Parameter
examples.description: Passes an output variable by reference.

→.name: Return Type
→.description: Separates a callable signature's parameters from its output type. Async callable carriers and body results are distinct; contracts describe the body result.

extends.name: Base Type
extends.description: Specifies a class's base type or inherited interfaces on an interface. Preserve generic arguments.

implements.name: Implemented Interface
implements.description: Specifies an interface implemented by a class or value type.

catch.name: Catch Block
catch.description: Catches exceptions with optional type, binder and filter. Its indented body follows try.

finally.name: Finally Block
finally.description: Runs the indented cleanup body on exit from try, including exceptions and returns.

get.name: Getter
get.description: Declares a property or indexer getter. An empty body is auto-implemented; an indented body contains statements.

init.name: Init Accessor
init.description: Declares an initialization-only property accessor. Preserve its visibility and body.

base.name: Base Constructor or Member
base.description: As the first constructor clause, calls the base constructor. In expressions, selects a base member.

this.name: Receiver, Constructor, Indexer or Extension Parameter
this.syntax: this.Member; this(args); this[int:index] → Type; this Type:receiver
this.description: Selects the current instance, delegates to another constructor as its first clause, declares an indexer, or marks the first extension-method parameter. These contexts are distinct.
this.csharpEquivalent: this.Member; : this(args); Type this[int index]; this Type receiver

case.name: Match Arm
case.syntax: case pattern → result; case pattern with indented statements
case.description: Declares an ordered expression or statement match arm. Use _ for a default pattern; preserve guards.

in.name: Iteration Source or Readonly Parameter
in.syntax: each item in source; in Type:value
in.description: Introduces a collection iteration source, or marks a readonly reference parameter in a signature.
in.csharpEquivalent: foreach (var item in source); in Type value

out.name: Output Parameter
out.description: Declares an output parameter in a signature. At a call site, pass the output argument with out.

from.name: Snapshot Range Start
from.syntax: for i from start to end step delta
from.description: Starts a counted loop whose start, end and step are evaluated once, in order.

to.name: Inclusive Snapshot Range End
to.syntax: for i from start to end step delta
to.description: Sets the inclusive endpoint of a snapshot counted loop. This is not a half-open slicing range.

step.name: Snapshot Range Step
step.syntax: for i from start to end step delta
step.description: Sets the snapshot range increment. Omission means +1; zero throws, and checked overflow ends iteration.

??.name: Null-Coalescing Expression
??.description: Evaluates the fallback only when the left operand is null.

?..name: Null-Conditional Access
?..description: Accesses the member only when the receiver is not null.

when.name: Pattern Guard or Catch Filter
when.syntax: case var name when condition → result; catch Type:name when condition
when.description: Adds a pattern guard or an exception filter. Evaluate it only after the corresponding pattern or exception selection.
when.csharpEquivalent: case var name when condition: statements; catch (Type name) when (condition)

add.name: Event Add Accessor
add.syntax: event Handler:Changed with an indented add body
add.description: Declares the custom event subscription accessor. Pair it with remove and preserve all statements.

remove.name: Event Remove Accessor
remove.syntax: event Handler:Changed with an indented remove body
remove.description: Declares the custom event unsubscription accessor. Pair it with add and preserve all statements.

primer.introduction:
# Calor syntax exemplar (reference sheet)

Calor compiles to C# on .NET 10. Indent bodies two spaces; structural blocks end at dedent.
Declarations use lowercase, space-separated headers without source IDs. Tooling maintains identity.
Ordinary calls use parentheses; lambdas use => with an expression or indented statement body.

Every complete module in the "Complete programs" section below must compile under the same
strict policy used by calor_compile. The fragments summarize supported forms; they are not programs.

## Core syntax

```
module Name                          Module
func Name (string:x) → string        Public by default; private is explicit
!                                    Pure row; cw console write; fs:r/fs:w file I/O;
                                     mut collection/heap mutation; alloc allocation
let string:name = expression         Immutable (type optional)
var int:name = 0                     Mutable (type optional)
set name expression                 Updates, including increments expressed as addition
requires condition / => condition   Precondition / postcondition (result = body return value)
return expression                   Return (bare return for void)
Console.WriteLine(expression)        Print line [needs cw]
if condition / else if condition / else
                                     Indented branches
while condition                     Condition checked before each iteration
for i from 0 to 9 step 1             Inclusive snapshot range; bounds evaluated once
for i = 0; i < Bound(); i = i + 1    Condition reevaluated on every test
each item in collection             Collection iteration (optional type:item)
each key, value in dictionary        Synchronous two-name deconstruction
```

Expressions use infix operators with C# precedence: a + b, a == b, p && q,
!p, i < n, n % 3, value ?? fallback and condition ? yes : no.
Binary operators associate left; ?? and ?: associate right. Boolean operators short circuit.
Use !condition || consequence for implication, not a special operator. Newlines end expressions.
Use C# type names, T[] arrays, T? nullability and literals such as 42, true, "hi", 18.00m and 1.5f.
Escapes include \", \n and \r. Plain strings interpolate "Hello ${name}";
"\${0}" keeps literal placeholder text. Use nullability and exceptions for absence/failure,
not dedicated Option/Result forms.

## Calls

```
Obj.Method(arg1, arg2)                     Postfix call; comma-separated arguments
let string[]:lines = File.ReadAllLines(path)
File.AppendAllText(path, key + "=" + value + "\n")
let bool:ok = File.Exists(path)
let int:n = LocalFunc(x)                   User functions use the same call syntax
let Func<int,int>:twice = (int:x) => x * 2
```

Callees may be expressions; calls, member access and indexing can chain.
Only methods use parentheses; property/field reads use obj.Property.
Do not write structural closers or brace bodies for indented lambdas.

## Strings

```
s.Length                           s.Substring(start, count)
s.Contains(sub)                    s.IndexOf(sub, StringComparison.Ordinal)
s.StartsWith(prefix)               s.Replace(oldValue, newValue)
s.Trim()   s.ToUpper()   s.ToLower()   a.Equals(b)   s.EndsWith(suffix)
let string:letter = line.Substring(i, 1)    One-character string, not a char
let char:character = line[i]               A character
```

Preserve argument counts and comparison modes; do not invent overloads or replace an explicit
ordinal comparison with a culture-dependent overload. Ordinary method names do not capture calls.

## Lists and dictionaries

```
let List<string>:items = new List<string>()
items.Add(value)                            Append [needs mut]
let int:n = items.Count
let string:element = items[i]
let Dictionary<string,int>:ages = new Dictionary<string,int>()
set ages[key] value                         Upsert, not Add [needs mut]
```

Collection mutation needs mut; allocation needs alloc; file I/O needs fs:r, fs:w or fs:rw.
Callers declare at least the union of their callees' effects. Unknown effects are not purity proofs.
Source-generic receiver metadata must resolve honestly; do not add casts or fake types to obtain
an effect charge. Arrays and lists differ: File.ReadAllLines returns string[], not List<string>.
primer.mistakes:
## Common mistakes (these do NOT compile — shown so you avoid them)

```
=> RESULT >= 0       wrong; the return value is lowercase: => result >= 0
if                   wrong; if needs a condition, such as if x > 0
if {x > 0}           wrong; braces do not surround conditions
```

Blocks end at dedent; structural closing tags and section headers are retired.
Write `else` or `else if` for a branch. Declaration IDs belong in the project
`.calor/ids.json` sidecar, never in the source signature. Use an ordinary header:
`func Add (int:a, int:b) → int`.

Effects: `! cw` declares console write. Declare effects on functions that perform I/O.
See `calor://effects` for the full effect catalog.

catalogs.type-mappings.md:
# C# types in Calor

Use the same C# names: `int`, `long`, `short`, `sbyte`, `byte`, `ushort`, `uint`,
`ulong`, `float`, `double`, `decimal`, `string`, `bool`, `char`, `object`, `void`.
Arrays use `T[]` (jagged arrays: `T[][]`); nullable values/references use `T?`.
Use ordinary .NET generic types such as `List<T>`, `Dictionary<K,V>`, `HashSet<T>`,
`IEnumerable<T>`, `Task<T>` and `Func<T,R>`, not dedicated absence/failure types.
Declare an async function with `func Name async (...) → Task<T>` and use `await` in its body.

Types and value construction are distinct: `let List<int>:items = new List<int>()`
binds a collection value. A collection initializer such as `new List<int>{1, 2}`
is an expression, not a type name. `File.ReadAllLines(path)` returns `string[]`,
not `List<string>`.
